speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, please tell me how many episodes you have had in the last 24 hours and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of levofloxacin use is significant. Have you experienced any muscle weakness, tingling sensations, or difficulty seeing clearly since starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the cramping and discomfort. Given your recent use of levofloxacin for pneumonia, is there any possibility of a Clostridioides difficile infection? Additionally, have you noticed any severe dehydration symptoms like dizziness or very dry mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection.

The clinical picture of acute watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping in a patient recently treated with levofloxacin is highly suggestive of *C. difficile*. Please proceed with the following diagnostic workup: REQUEST TEST: C. difficile toxin assay.
